newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Euro-MPs target Commission pay over mismanagement.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs target Commission pay over mismanagement.

text.p: Members of the European Parliament want to freeze 10 percent of the salaries of European Commissioners in 1997 to force them to clear up allegations of mismanagement in the department responsible for tourism policy.

The Parliament's Budget Committee, seeking the assembly's backing for the move when it votes later in October, wants the tourism directorate restructured to ensure there is no reoccurrence of the scandal.

Belgium has asked for the diplomatic immunity of department's director general, Heinrich Von Moltke, to be lifted as part of its enquiries. The European Commission has refused the request. Two other officials of the directorate have left the Commission.

"These means are being put into the reserve to encourage the European Commission as a political organ to take immediate measures to keep new cases of mismanagement in the organisation of its administration from happening," the budget committee said in a statement.

The commissioner responsible for tourism, Christos Papoutsis, condemned the move. He said the allegations were being investigated and dated from before the current Commission, headed by Jacques Santer, took office in January 1995.

"It is unacceptable that certain cases which, on the initiative of the Commission are already being dealt with by the competent legal authorities, are being used to attack the policies in favour of small and medium enterprises and tourism," he said in a statement.
"The irregularities under discussion are relics of the past and do not concern the Santer Commission," he added.
